mechanism: Foscarnet causes dose-dependent renal tubular dysfunction and can impair potassium reabsorption, leading to hypokalemia, while concurrent potassium supplementation may be necessary but requires careful monitoring due to risk of hyperkalemia if renal function deteriorates.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels frequently during foscarnet therapy and adjust potassium supplementation based on renal function and electrolyte concentrations; assess for signs of hypo- or hyperkalemia.
